This assertion is incorrect because it assumes an additional 1000 bytes per write operation, which is not accounted for in the code. The actual number of bytes written should be exactly `2 * fourGB` if no additional data is being added.

The implementation introduces handlers `DiscardingReadsHandler` and `DiscardingWritesAndFlushesHandler` that discard inbound and outbound data without any logging or metrics. This lack of observability makes it impossible to trace when data is being discarded, leading to debugging difficulties and potential issues in understanding the behavior of the system during tests.

The test method `writePcapGreaterThan4Gb` uses a large number of iterations (`(fourGB / chunkSize) + 2`) to write data, which can lead to performance issues and increased test execution time. This is not optimal for resource efficiency and may cause the test suite to run slowly or timeout.

The casting of long values to int in `writePacket` does not handle the case where the segment or acknowledgment numbers exceed the uint32 max value. The code assumes that the values will always be within the valid range after wrapping, but there is no explicit check or handling for cases where they might exceed this range due to invalid inputs or other issues, leading to potential overflow in TCP packets.

The method `incrementUintSegmentNumber` does not include any validation or error handling for cases where the input values are negative or exceed expected ranges. This could lead to unexpected behavior if invalid inputs are passed to this method, posing potential security vulnerabilities and incorrect sequence numbers.

@normanmaurer I'll have time today to look into this and address any issues I find.

Found 2 issues directly related to this PR while using Wireshark to look at the generated 5GB pcap. Those will be addressed.

Noticed two other issues present in 4.1.

1. If the payload is larger than 65495 for TCP, the length field in the IP packet is incorrect due to the length being a ushort. UDP will have a similar problem.
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/155cec08-767f-4efc-a2c5-c9c04718bd75)
2. When the PcapWriteHandler is attached to a TCP server, the FIN messages have incorrect segment and ack numbers. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/236c3109-558d-4fa2-8cce-5fa05503ebc0)


I will try to find the time to address these here with unit tests

For TCP, the payload can just be split into multiple PCAP entries. 
For UDP, I imagine it could just log that it received too large of a payload.
Alright, all of the above have been handled. Tested large PCAP files and those show correctly in Wireshark now.
